key_insight: A population balance model can directly track pore-size evolution during freeze-drying microcollapse and link it to mass-transfer resistance with near-standard computational cost.
engineering_relevance: This gives freeze-drying engineers a predictive way to estimate product temperature and collapse risk without relying on ad hoc empirical resistance fits.
method: Model the pore-size distribution with a population balance equation.
Reduce the dynamics using method of moments with interpolative closure.
Convert pore evolution into a resistance-to-mass-transfer relation for primary drying.
evidence_signal: The model was validated against multiple literature datasets, including temperature-dependent cases, post-hoc pore-size measurements, and a multi-experiment fit that matched product temperatures across conditions.
watch_item: The microcollapse rate may behave like a material parameter, but it still requires calibration and its transferability across formulations should be checked carefully.
paper_title: Direct Modeling of Pore Size Evolution and Microcollapse in Lyophilization by Population Balance
